studies.lifeInProphetsTime: The pilgrimage season brought tribes into the valley from across the peninsula, and it was the one time of year when a message could reach beyond the city. Meeting arrivals on the approach roads was therefore an effective response, since a traveller warned at the last well would arrive already prepared to dismiss what he heard. Control of the roads was control of the audience.
studies.didYouKnow: Both distinctive words in this passage occur only here in the whole Quran, the one for the dividers and the one for what they made of the recitation. The Quran elsewhere records a different complaint about how this Book was treated, in which the Messenger tells his Lord that his people abandoned it, using an image of desertion rather than dismemberment.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Dividing something is presented as a way of neutralising it. A message taken whole has to be accepted or refused, while a message broken into pieces can be handled piece by piece, and each fragment answered separately. That applies to scripture and to hearing itself. The oath that closes the passage answers it directly: the questioning will cover everything a person did, taken together rather than fragment by fragment.

crossReferences.why: Records the other complaint about this Book, that his own people abandoned it entirely.
Gives the same role in its earliest form, the command to arise and warn.
States the questioning this oath promises, of the peoples sent to and of the messengers alike.

studies.applyIt: Notice whether you take the Quran in pieces you already agree with. Most of us have a working selection: the consoling verses, the ones that support our positions. This week read a whole surah from beginning to end, including the parts you usually pass over quickly, and let it stand as one thing.

studies.title: We Suffice You Against Them
studies.meaning: An instruction to speak out is paired with an instruction to turn away, and both are given at once. Then a guarantee about the mockers, followed by something rarer: an acknowledgement that the words are having an effect. We know your chest tightens at what they say. The response prescribed is not argument and not endurance in silence but glorification and prostration. Commentators note that what is offered for a social injury is a physical act of worship rather than a change of feeling.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. The classical sources connect this instruction with the beginning of open public preaching, after a period in which the message had spread more quietly, and they differ over how long that earlier period lasted. Mockery from the leading families is well attested for these years, and the Quran addresses it repeatedly in surahs from this period.

keyTerms.note: The verb for cleaving something so it separates, used of dawn breaking and of glass cracking. Applied to speech it means saying a thing so plainly that the matter divides around it.
A physical description of distress rather than a metaphor for sadness. The Quran locates the pressure of hostility in the body, which is why the remedy offered is also something done with the body.
The participle names a group rather than the act, so the instruction is to be among them. Belonging is prescribed alongside the posture, which matters for someone whose community had turned on him.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Ridicule was a weapon with real force in a society organised around honour. Satirical verse could damage a man's standing across the peninsula, and being laughed at in the assembly cost more than being argued with. Mockers were not a nuisance in that setting; they were doing something effective, and everyone in the audience knew what it was costing the man they were aimed at.
studies.didYouKnow: The Quran addresses this particular pressure more than once and always joins the remedy to praise. One passage tells him to endure what they say and to glorify his Lord before sunrise and before sunset. Another says he is before God's eyes and tells him to proclaim his Lord's praises when he rises. A short surah addressed to him opens by asking whether his chest was not expanded.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Distress is acknowledged rather than corrected, which is unusual. Nothing here tells the one addressed that he should not feel the pressure or that the mockery does not matter. The instruction moves instead to something he can do, and the prescription is bodily and repeatable. That treats a wounded state as something worked through by action rather than resolved by argument, and it locates the relief in worship rather than in vindication.

crossReferences.why: Joins the same instruction to endure what they say with praise before sunrise and sunset.
Names the same tightening of the chest and connects it to their demands for a treasure or an angel.
Opens by asking whether his chest was not expanded, and pairs hardship with ease twice.

studies.applyIt: The next time criticism lands and stays with you, do not reason with it. Do something physical and prescribed instead: pray two units, walk a fixed distance, read a page aloud. The remedy in this passage is an action rather than a thought, and it works on the state rather than on the argument.
